messages:
morgan: Quick RFC follow-up — proposal to start pruning the monolith by extracting the ingest pipeline (model/asset ingestion + validation) into a standalone service. Outline: 1) extractor service owning ingest flows, 2) clear async contract (events + dead-letter), 3) migration window with proxy pass-through, 4) observability/SLAs. Looking for concerns and rollout ideas.

jamie: +1 on splitting ingest. main question: how do we migrate DB ownership? currently a single ingestion_state table is used by runtime.

morgan: plan is phased: read-only replicas for extractor, shadow-writes from runtime to new store for 2 weeks, then cutover. DB schema will be namespaced (ingest.*). no destructive migration until cutover.

sara: observability: we need trace continuity and cost attribution. extractor needs to emit trace ids and token counts. also suggest a health-check endpoint returning last-processed-offset.

kai: what about KV cache and prefix caching? ingest currently primes several KV keys used by runtime. extractor should provide a compatible cache priming API or a short-lived priming job. worried about latency spikes on cutover.

morgan: agreed. propose extractor exposes /prime?key=... and runtime will fall back to on-demand generation for 24h after cutover. also enable gradual traffic % via feature flag.

lina: can we reuse the existing ingest worker code as-is behind a service boundary first? i.e., lift-and-shift into a new binary to reduce initial risk.

morgan: yes — phase 0 is lift-and-shift containerization with identical behavior + sidecar proxy. phase 1 is contract hardening and async eventing.

jamie: DB migration script sketch: \n```sql\nBEGIN;\nALTER TABLE ingestion_state RENAME TO ingestion_state_old;\nCREATE TABLE ingest_state (id uuid, namespace text, state jsonb, PRIMARY KEY(id));\n-- shadow write population job runs for N days\nCOMMIT;\n```\n\nwill add a backfill job. needs runbook.

devops-bot: deploy plan requested: create canary cluster 'ingest-prune-canary', route 1% of new ingestion requests. schedule maintenance window if cutover requires write lock.

sara: we should also add evals: pre/post quality checks on a sample of ingested assets (hash and validation). if quality drops, auto-roll back traffic.

kai: concerns: cross-service auth. current internal tokens are opaque. extractor needs a scoped service account + mTLS. ops must ensure key rotation is supported.

morgan: noted. security checklist: scoped SA, mTLS, KMS integration for secrets, audit events. i'll add to RFC.

lina: testing notes: local run using docker-compose to simulate proxy, include flaky network tests and DB latency injector.

jamie: rollout timeline proposal: 2 weeks phase0 (lift+canary), 3 weeks shadow writes + metrics, 1 week cutover window. total ~6 weeks.

morgan: thanks — i'll update RFC with timeline and a rollback plan (traffic switch + DB failback). tagging @eng-sre for runbook and @security for review. :eyes:

devops-bot: runbook request created: https://go/redwood/runbooks/PRUNE-INGEST-2026 (automated ticket #4582).

sara: :thumbsup: add SLA targets (p99 latency before/after) so we can measure regressions.

kai: also add cost estimate: expected small increase in inter-service traffic and new infra for extractor (1-2 instances initially).

morgan: will include cost bump in the doc and propose opt-in tiering for non-critical customers during the migration. thanks all.

lina: small nit — update API semver header on proxy for compatibility checks.

morgan: noted, will include API contract example in RFC.

jamie: LGTM overall. excited to chip away at monolith debt. :raised_hands:
